## 235. Batch 233 step (b) - the four money ports (13 edges -> 0)

### 235.1 What the ratchet said, and what was done

The owner's step (b): "ports for RidePayout, NoShowSettlement, CashRideFeeService and
PaymentStrategyFactory (13 sites; CancellationRefundInterface already exists)". The ratchet's message named
all 13 `file :: class` pairs and they were exactly the RIDE -> MONEY pair - no other pair moved in this step.

Two of the four were already behind an interface; the interfaces were simply not used by RIDE, and the
surfaces RIDE needs were missing. So two existing ports were EXTENDED and three new ones written:

| port | status | surface RIDE actually calls |
|---|---|---|
| `App\Interfaces\Payment\RidePayoutInterface` | existed, extended | `releaseEscrowToDriver` (already there) + `releaseEarningsToDriver(Ride, Collection)` |
| `App\Interfaces\Payment\CancellationRefundInterface` | existed, extended | the two refunds (already there) + `calculateRefundPolicy(Carbon, Carbon)` + `processTimeBasedCancellation(Booking, Ride, int, array)` |
| `App\Interfaces\Payment\NoShowSettlementInterface` | new | `processPassengerNoShow`, `processDriverNoShowRefund` |
| `App\Interfaces\Payment\CashRideFeeServiceInterface` | new | `refundCashRideCreationFee`, `canCreateCashRide`, `chargeCashRideCreationFee` |
| `App\Interfaces\Payment\PaymentStrategyFactoryInterface` | new | `make(string\|PaymentMethod)` |

`NoShowSettlement`, `CashRideFeeService` and `PaymentStrategyFactory` now `implement` those interfaces; no
method body changed. The three new ports are bound in `registerBoundaryPorts()` to the same singletons
registered earlier, so instance identity and construction order are unchanged.

One deliberate signature decision: `PaymentStrategyFactoryInterface::make()` declares **no return type**.
The concrete return is `App\Domain\Payment\Strategies\PaymentStrategy`, and naming that in the shared kernel
would make the kernel depend on MONEY. PHP permits an interface method with no return type to be implemented
by one that narrows it, so the dependency stays one-way (RIDE -> `App\Interfaces` -> MONEY) and callers
receive the identical strategy object. The concrete type is documented in the interface's `@return`.

The eight RIDE files switched type-hint and import only: `BookingCancellationService` (CancellationRefund),
`BookingService` (CancellationRefund, PaymentStrategyFactory), `BookingCompletionService`
(PaymentStrategyFactory), `NoShowPenaltyService` (NoShowSettlement), `Noshowservice` (NoShowSettlement),
`RideCancellationService` (CancellationRefund, CashRideFeeService), `RideCompletionService` (RidePayout,
CashRideFeeService), `RideService` (CancellationRefund, RidePayout, CashRideFeeService). The inner
`new BookingCancellationService(...)` / `new BookingCompletionService(...)` / `new NoShowPenaltyService(...)`
constructions keep their argument order and now simply pass port-typed objects to port-typed parameters.

Two deliberate signature decisions, both recorded in the interfaces themselves:

### 236.3 The moves, and why each was needed

1. **`DuplicateNationalIdException` -> `App\Exceptions\Domain`** (kernel), as instructed. Import updated in

3. **`PassengerWalletCharger` -> `App\Services\Payment`**, as instructed, **plus a port**. The move alone

4. **`ProfileController` no longer calls `ScoreController::formatScore`.** The body moved verbatim into

   delegate** - `RideLifecycleHandler` still calls it and `RoutesIntegrityTest` pins it in
   `UNROUTED_BY_DESIGN` - so the method survives with identical output and the IDENTITY -> RIDE edge is gone.
5. **`ScoreBounds` -> `App\Domain\Score`** holds `START_SCORE = 70`, `MIN_SCORE = 0`, `MAX_SCORE = 100`.
   The instruction named `MIN_SCORE`, but `ScoreLedger` also read `MAX_SCORE` (both ends of its one clamp)

### 237.1 Task 1 - one distinct error kind, and it is not RV-46

Baseline run: `php vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Feature tests/Unit --no-coverage` ->
`Tests: 2598, Assertions: 6848, Errors: 24, Skipped: 2`.

The 24 are 20 x `Tests\Unit\Services\Payment\CashRideFeeServiceTest` + 4 x
`Tests\Unit\Services\Payment\L18CashRideFeeOutcomeLedgerTest`, and they are **one** distinct kind:

```
Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException: SQLSTATE[23000]: Integrity constraint
violation: 1062 Duplicate entry '0912345678' for key 'wallets.wallets_phone_number_unique'
(SQL: insert into `wallets` (`name`, `phone_number`, `balance`, ...) values (Primary Escrow, 0912345678, 100, ...))
```

Thrown from each victim's `setUp()`, which does an unconditional
`Wallet::create(['name' => 'Primary Escrow', 'phone_number' => config('admin.system_admin.phone'), ...])`.
No second kind, no tier assertion, no stale constructor: the app is correct, the fixture collides.
**Not RV-46** - RV-46 is the refund-tier divergence, and after this fix all 20 tests in
`CashRideFeeServiceTest` pass, so no tier test is red either. In isolation both files are green
(`tests/Unit/Services/Payment` -> `OK (24 tests, 52 assertions)`; `tests/Unit` -> `OK (977 tests, 1528
assertions)`), so the colliding row has to be committed by an earlier Feature test in the same process.

### 237.2 Root cause - `RV45RideNotFoundTest` commits the three system wallets it seeds

`tests/Feature/Review/RV45RideNotFoundTest::faultOnRideRead()` drops `rides.available_seats` to force a
real `QueryException`. That is DDL, and MySQL implicitly COMMITS the open `RefreshDatabase` transaction
when DDL runs - the class's own batch-229 docblock says exactly that, and `deleteCommittedFixtures()`
exists to delete what the commit leaked. It deleted the driver, wallet, profile, photos, refresh tokens,
ride and signup rating - and missed the three system wallets `seedSystemWallets(10_000_000)` creates in
`setUp()`.

Two independent pieces of evidence, neither a guess:

1. **After** the baseline run the shared schema held exactly three `wallets` rows, all `user_id NULL`,
   `name NULL`, balances `10,000,000` / `10,000,000` / `0` on phones `0912345678` (`system_admin`),
   `0987654321` (`sycash`) and `0900000042` (`external`) - the exact shape of
   `SeedsSystemWallets::seedSystemWallets()` (`firstOrCreate` without a `name`). JUnit per-test timings
   plus the XML's own mtime place a class boundary at `+278s` into the run, and the three rows are
   stamped `02:09:26`; the class starting at `+278s` is `Tests\Feature\Review\RV45RideNotFoundTest`.
2. **Causal, same command before and after the change:**
   `php vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Feature/Review/RV45RideNotFoundTest.php tests/Unit/Services/Payment`
   -> before `Tests: 28, Assertions: 14, Errors: 24`; after `OK (28 tests, 66 assertions)`; and the
   schema after the run holds **0** `wallets` rows where it held 3 before.

Fix, commit `fd1dac1` (test construction only, root cause - no assertion edited, no app code touched):
one block added to `deleteCommittedFixtures()` deleting `wallets` where `user_id IS NULL` and
`phone_number IN (...)` for the three reserved phones, built through `array_filter` so an unset config
phone cannot widen the delete.

**Residual recorded, not changed:** the two victims still do a blind `Wallet::create()`; any future test
that commits a wallet on a reserved phone will red them again. Making them `firstOrCreate`-based is a
separate, optional hardening and was not done here.

### 237.5 The 19 schema-level errors in the first post-fix Feature-first run: a measuring artifact

That first post-fix Feature-first run reported `Errors: 19` - 9 x
`Tests\Feature\Payment\WalletTransactionServiceTest` and 10 x `Tests\Feature\Profile\ProfileTest`, all
`Illuminate\Database\QueryException`, with **zero** name overlap with the 24. Two messages:

```
Base table or view not found: 1146 Table 't3_batch.wallets' doesn't exist
Column not found: 1054 Unknown column 'token_version' in 'field list'   (insert into `users` ...)
```

Cause: a second phpunit process was started against the same shared scratch database while the full
suite was mid-run. That scoped run was `php vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Feature/AppFuture` (10 s), and
`tests/Feature/AppFuture/UntangleBatchTest` uses `RefreshDatabase`, so it ran `migrate:fresh` - dropping
and re-creating every table under the running suite. The window explains both messages exactly: `wallets`
is absent between the drop and its re-creation, and `users` is re-created by an early migration and only
receives `token_version` from a later one. The errors cluster at `02:29:20`, exactly when that scoped run
executed; the JUnit shows no slow or hung test (slowest class 111 s, slowest single test 9.7 s); and the
clean re-run with nothing else touching the database is green in both orderings.

**Lesson recorded: the scratch database is ONE shared resource. Never start a second phpunit or artisan
process against it while a suite is in flight - scoped runs included.**

### 238.2 The harness - four rules that make a snapshot mean something

`tests/Feature/Snapshots/ApiSnapshotTestCase.php` builds the same world for every case: the three
system wallets (1,000,000 each), a driver / passenger / other / wallet-less user, their three
wallets and tokens, one active e-pay ride, and the six actors (`driver`, `passenger`, `other`,
`walletless`, `admin` = SYSTEM_ADMIN, `staff` = SUPPORT_AGENT, `staff_admin` = ADMIN). External
services are faked per case (openrouteservice, mapbox, nominatim, FCM, `*`), so no test can reach
the network.

`SnapshotNormaliser` replaces everything that is not a fact of the response: ids, timestamps,
tokens, e-mails, UUIDs, redacted values, uploaded file URLs, and any timestamp EMBEDDED in a longer
string (the escalation note carries `[ESCALATED by X at 2026-10-31 16:08:47]`, which drifted between
runs until the rule existed). `time_only`, `date_only` and `*_human` / `*_formatted` are timestamps
too.

Two rules were added after the net caught itself:

1. **Update mode refuses to write when the status is not the documented one.** A red generation run
   had recorded a 3-query budget for `rides/create-with-route` from a 422 short-circuit, poisoning
   the baseline downward for the real path. `SNAPSHOT_UPDATE=1` now fails without writing unless
   `status === expect`, so a red run cannot write anything at all.
2. **An unresolved placeholder is a failure, not an empty id.** `/api/complaints//show` and
   `/api/staff/complaints//escalate` silently matched a DIFFERENT route (the index) and pinned that
   body under the misleading name. `resolvePlaceholders()` now fails when a `{name}` has no
   non-empty value, naming the placeholder and the case.

### 238.3 Deliverable 2 - the query budgets, shrink-only

`tests/Snapshots/query-budgets.json` records, per case, the `DB::getQueryLog()` count of the
generating (green) run. `AssertsApiSnapshot` fails when a run exceeds it, and prints a `STDERR`
hint when a run comes in UNDER it. `QueryBudgetStore::record()` can only lower a number (`min()`),
so a normal run cannot raise a baseline even in update mode. 152 cases, 152 budgets. One budget
failure was real and is recorded as a finding (238.5, item 2).

### 238.4 Deliverable 4 - the leak guard, at its source

`tests/Support/CommittedRowLeakDetector.php` counts seven tables (`wallets`, `users`, `rides`,
`bookings`, `user_ratings`, `profile_comments`, `refresh_tokens`) after each test class and throws
`RuntimeException: COMMITTED-ROW LEAK after Class::test: ...` naming the table and row count.
`GuardsAgainstCommittedLeaks` registers the check AFTER `parent::setUp()`, which is what makes it
work: `RefreshDatabase` registers its rollback in `beforeApplicationDestroyed`, and Laravel runs
those callbacks in registration order, so a callback registered later observes the database AFTER
the rollback. A class that should have rolled back and did not is therefore caught at that class,
not in whichever later test trips over the leftovers - the RV45 pollution pattern cannot recur
silently.

### 238.5 The net's findings - five defects it caught, four fixed inside the tests

The point of a safety net is that it finds things. It did:

1. **`GET /api/staff/chat/conversations/{id}/messages` answers 500 for every conversation.**
   `StaffChatController::messages()` formats through `formatConversation()`, which reads
   `$conversation->latestMessage`, and `ChatRepository::findConversation()` does not eager-load that
   relation. The lazy-loading guard turns the N+1 into a hard failure. This is an app defect, not a
   test artefact, and it cannot be fixed from a test, so the route is **parked** with that reason
   instead of being pinned to a 500 that would hide it. **Owner action offered, not taken (no
   `app/` changes in this batch): eager-load `latestMessage` in `findConversation()`.**
2. **`Tests\Feature\Review\OtpDisclosureTest` committed `otps` rows.** It extended
   `Tests\TestCase` without any rollback trait, so the OTPs its cases send stayed in the shared
   scratch database; the next snapshot run's `auth/otp-verify-invalid` case then read 2 queries
   where its budget said 1. Root cause fixed by giving the class `RefreshDatabase`, and the two
   snapshot cases that depend on an empty `otps` table now clear it explicitly (`clearOtpRows()`).
3. **`/api/complaints/{id}` and `/api/staff/complaints/{id}` were snapshotting the INDEX route.**
   The complaint id was read from `data.id`; the store envelope puts it at `complaint.id`, so the
   substitution was empty and the URI collapsed to `.../complaints//`. Fixed at the source (correct
   envelope path) and guarded for the future (238.2, rule 2).
4. **Three list routes returned rows in a different ORDER between the generating run and the
   verifying run** (`/api/admin/users`, `/api/admin/wallets`, `/api/admin/trips`). The whole world is
   created inside one second, so `ORDER BY created_at` had ties and MySQL was free to answer
   either way. Fixed in the fixture, not the app: `staggerWorldTimestamps()` gives every world row a
   distinct, well-separated `created_at`.
5. **A red update run poisoned a budget** (238.2, rule 1) - the guard, not the app.

### 238.6 Deliverable 3 - the ledger property tests

`tests/Feature/Payment/LedgerInvariantsPropertyTest.php` checks four movements - booking charge,
payout, driver-cancellation refund, passenger no-show - against three amounts (`50,000.00`,
`1,000.50` the RV-19 odd tenth, `33.33`), 12 tests, and asserts four PROPERTIES rather than one row
list:

| property | assertion |
|---|---|
| debits equal credits | `SUM(ledger_entries.amount) = 0` after every movement |
| money is conserved | `SUM(wallets.balance)` is unchanged by the movement |
| escrow is never negative | no `bookings.escrow_held < 0`, and it returns to exactly `0.00` after release |
| posting key is idempotent | replaying the movement raises `/already posted/` and moves NOTHING: same ledger rows, same transaction rows, same balances, same escrow |

The replay assertions run AFTER the exception inside a `try/catch` (not `expectException`), so
"nothing moved" is actually executed rather than being unreachable dead code.

### 238.7.1 What the FIRST full pass found, and why it was a fixture fix, not an app fix

The snapshot corpus was green in isolation and 9 of its cases were red in the first full-suite run.

### 239. Stage 0.5 - hardening the stage-0 safety net (owner goal; tests only, except ONE app line)

Stage 0 built the net; this stage makes it hard to fool. Steps 1-8, one commit each, `SNAPSHOT_UPDATE=1`
allowed for exactly one regeneration run (step 3) plus the single new case in step 2.

#### 239.1 Step 1 - every snapshot call asserts the route it actually matched

`snapshotCall()` now takes the route the case DECLARES and, after the call, compares it with
`app('router')->current()` as `METHOD uri-pattern`. A case whose placeholder resolved to nothing
(an empty complaint id collapsed `/api/complaints//show` onto the index route) or whose URI was
subtly wrong used to pin the WRONG route body under the RIGHT route name and stay green. A request
that matched no route at all now fails too, with the declared route named.

Non-vacuity: flipping `misc/ping`'s declared route to `POST api/ping` produced
"declares POST api/ping but the request matched GET api/ping"; the probe file was reverted in the
same step (`git status` clean for it).

#### 239.2 Step 2 - the parked staff chat route: ONE app line, and the route is live

The defect stage 0 parked: `GET /api/staff/chat/conversations/{id}/messages` answered 500 on every
conversation. Root cause was a chain of missing eager loads, all reached from
`ChatRepository::findConversation()`, which loaded only `participants`:

1. `formatConversation()` reads `$conversation->latestMessage` (first 500),
2. then `$otherUser?->profile?->profile_photo` on a participant (second 500),
3. then `$lastMessage->sender?->first_name` (third 500).

The fix is ONE line in that method:

```php
return Conversation::with('participants.profile', 'latestMessage.sender')->find($conversationId);
```

The route is out of the parked list (5 parked, 149 snapshotted, totals `api_routes: 154`), has a case
(`staff/chat-messages`, budget 13 queries) and answers 200.

**One deliberate query-budget rise, disclosed:** `staff/chat-send` went 15 -> 19 because it shares
`findConversation()` and now pays for the eager loads the read path needs (participants.profile,
latestMessage + its sender - constant per request, not an N+1; the count does not grow with the
number of participants). Shrink-only stays the rule for every other case; this single entry was
raised by hand with this reason. It was the only rise until step 3, which records fifteen more with
the owner's explicit approval (see 239.3).

#### 239.3 Step 3 - the normaliser's three rules, per-document aliases, and a corpus that is never empty

Owner constraints honoured: tests only (no `app/`, `config/`, `routes/`, migration or `phpunit.xml`
change in this step), `SNAPSHOT_UPDATE=1` used only for the regeneration, one phpunit process at a
time, no assertion edited, no budget raised without the owner's decision recorded below.

**The normaliser** (`tests/Support/Snapshots/SnapshotNormaliser.php`), now with nine DB-free unit
tests in `tests/Unit/Support/SnapshotNormaliserTest.php`:

1. Only a non-null SCALAR under a masked key is replaced. `id: null`, `updated_at: null` and an
   already-normalised `"<timestamp>"` stay exactly as the app sent them, so a fixture bug that stops
   populating a field on an ERROR path can no longer hide behind the mask.
2. Ids and emails get per-document aliases by first appearance: `<id:1>`, `<id:2>`, `<email:1>`.
   Before this, two different users both pinned as `<id>` and a snapshot could not tell "the same id
   twice" from "two different ids" - nor could a diff show that a relation changed owner.
3. Timestamps, tokens, uuids, stored filenames (`[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}`) and ids inside URL paths share
   the same first-appearance treatment, so a paginated `.../wallet/<id:1>/transactions` link and the
   `wallet.id` beside it are visibly the same id.

**The fixtures** (`ApiSnapshotTestCase`, `EngagementSnapshotTest`, `MiscSnapshotTest`,
`RidesSnapshotTest`): every list the owner named carries at least three rows, and every nested
collection that was empty carries at least one real row - profiles and four photos per account, three
live trips (each booked through the real endpoint), three future Damascus-Aleppo trips for the
search window, three score movements, three decided wallet requests, three admin wallet charges
written through the same two service calls the endpoint uses, three complaints with a real
attachment, profile comments, chat images with a metadata map. The world is built once in
`enrichWorld()` and costed once.

**A new gate, `SnapshotEmptinessTest`** (four tests, DB-free): ten mandated lists must carry >=3
items; twenty nested collections must carry >=1 row; any message list must contain a populated
`metadata` map; and any OTHER empty array in the whole corpus must appear in `EMPTY_BY_DESIGN` or
match `EMPTY_PATTERNS` with a written reason. The exemptions are genuine app behaviour, not
convenience: `chat/messages-store` and `staff/chat-send` return `metadata: []` for the TEXT type by
design (the image row in the same list pins the populated shape), and `profile/show` /
`profile/update` emit documents for the OWNER only (`ProfileController::ownerDocuments()` returns
`[]` for a non-owner view, and the update response formats through `formatProfileData()` with the
default `$isOwner = false` at `ProfileController:348`) - `profile/verify-status` pins the populated
map instead.

**The category report**, `C:\temp\snapshot-diff.php` against a byte copy of the committed corpus
(153 cases compared, 40 byte-identical, 113 files changed):

| Category | Count | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| STATUS | 0 | no case changed its HTTP status |
| ALIAS | 263 | `<id>` -> `<id:1>`, `<email>` -> `<email:1>`, plus ids inside pagination URLs |
| NEW-ITEMS | 207 | lists that gained rows (`1 -> 3 items`) and new nested keys |
| NULL | 54 | null <-> value flips, both directions |
| NUMBER | 98 | balances, scores, counters, `previous_balance`/`new_balance` |
| ANYTHING ELSE | 137 | explained below, every one of them |

The 137 are five groups, no unexplained entries:

1. Month windows and labels (`May 2026` -> `Jan 2026`, `joined_label` June instead of October):
   the clock is pinned to 2026-06-15, so a six-month window ending "now" moved with it.
2. `data.documents`: `[]` -> `{face_id, back_id, license}` on `admin/driver-profile` and
   `profile/verify-status` - the collections this step was asked to populate.
3. List composition and ordering: the world now has a second and third driver and a platform-admin
   account, so `admin/drivers`, `admin/users`, `staff/users`, the verification queues and the
   efficiency deltas report different (correct) rows, and `trips`/`rides/index` lead with tomorrow's
   trip at 45,000 instead of today's at 50,000.
4. Money: the passenger's wallet carries the three admin charges (+67,500), `admin/reports` escrow
   moves 50,000 -> 70,000 because the extra Homs booking holds one more seat, and the External
   Capital system wallet reads -67,500 (by design: external money enters the ledger against that
   account, decision un3).
5. Two formatter observations, recorded as findings rather than fixed (app frozen):
   `admin/dashboard.recent_activities[].date` is a STRING for an old row and an OBJECT
   (`{human, raw}`) once the same row is recent - the field's type depends on recency;
   `staff/chat-messages.conversation.last_message.created_at_iso` lost its `+03:00` suffix because
   the whole ISO string now matches `<timestamp>` (cosmetic, deterministic).

**Two determinism defects the verifying run found, both in the fixtures, both fixed:** with three
rows the corpus stopped being order-stable. `admin/routes-popular` ordered Hama and Homs - identical
trip_count, passengers and percentage - by whatever MySQL felt like, so an isolated run pinned one

for the 21 tables this API sorts by (auth and queue tables are deliberately excluded), immediately
before each request and outside the measured query window. Both defects were proven gone by running
the affected cases twice, and then the whole suite twice: `OK (160 tests, 1468 assertions)` twice in
a row, from the same corpus.

**Owner decision, recorded verbatim: the fifteen query budgets that the mandated enrichment makes

#### 239.4 Step 4 - the ROWS behind every money and ride mutation, and the three determinism defects that uncovered

**Why a second kind of snapshot.** A response snapshot pins what a route RETURNED. It cannot see the
write: a route that reports `"status": "confirmed"` and forgets the escrow leg, or charges the wallet
but never writes the ledger, returns a byte-identical body. Step 4 pins the rows instead.

**What was built.** `tests/Support/Snapshots/StateSnapshotRepository.php` reads and writes
`tests/Snapshots/state/<case>.json` with the SAME canonical encoder the response corpus uses, and the
same asymmetry: written only under `SNAPSHOT_UPDATE=1`, compared byte-for-byte otherwise.
`AssertsApiSnapshot::assertStateSnapshot()` normalises the capture through the same normaliser, so ids
become aliases and timestamps are masked. `ApiSnapshotTestCase::captureMoneyAndRideState()` dumps six
tables for every case in `MONEY_AND_RIDE_MUTATION_CASES` (24 cases), after the request and outside the
measured query window:

| Table | Columns pinned |
|---|---|
| `wallets` | id, user_id, phone_number, kind, balance, cash_ride_debt |
| `wallet_transactions` | id, wallet_id, user_id, type, amount, previous_balance, new_balance, status, reference, posting_key |
| `ledger_entries` | id, wallet_id, wallet_transaction_id, amount |
| `wallet_requests` | id, user_id, wallet_id, type, amount, status |
| `bookings` | id, user_id, ride_id, seats, status, unit_price, amount_paid, escrow_held |
| `rides` | id, driver_id, status, available_seats, price_per_seat |

Deliberately excluded, with reasons: `wallet_transactions.transaction_id` (the fixture writes
`ADM-<user id>-<n>-snapshot`, and the raw id inside a string is not aliased, so it would leak the
counter - nothing serialises it anyway), `ledger_entries.description`, and every timestamp.

**The coverage is derived, not remembered.** `StateSnapshotCoverageTest` (3 tests, DB-free) collects
the case definitions from every module and requires that every non-GET case on a wallet, admin-wallet,
passenger-charge, ride, booking or staff-cancel route is listed AND has a committed state file. It
found four cases step 4 had not listed - `bookings/passenger-confirm`, `bookings/passenger-no-show`,
`rides/driver-no-show`, `wallet/verify-and-create-missing-session` - all of which do write money or a
ride. Two non-GET routes write nothing and are exempted WITH their reason in `READ_ONLY_POST_CASES`
(`rides/route-options` and `rides/search-post`: POST because the body carries a whole payload, not
because they mutate), and a third test proves every exemption names a real non-GET case, so the map
cannot silently swallow a route that starts writing later.

**Non-vacuity, proven in both directions.** Editing one `escrow_held` in
`tests/Snapshots/state/rides/book.json` turns the case red with the message that names the state file
(restored by regenerating that single case); deleting `tests/Snapshots/state/wallet/initiate.json`
turns the coverage test red by name (restored). A gate that cannot fail is not a gate.

**DEFECT 1 (the reason this step took three regenerations): the alias namespace depended on the
auto-increment counters.** The step-3 normaliser keyed the alias map by the raw NUMBER across the
whole document, and its own docblock admitted the consequence: "a user id and a wallet id that happen
to be the same number look equal inside one response". Independent sequences collide in a YOUNG
database and diverge in a mature one, and the suite's own history decides how far each counter has
drifted - so a run of five snapshot modules (rather than nine) rewrote THIRTEEN snapshots that the
full run had just verified green. `rides/index.json` showed the mechanism exactly: a rating id pinned
`<id:4>` and the ride id `<id:2>` in one run, and the two SWAPPED in the next, because in the shorter
process `user_ratings.id` and `users.id` were both small enough to be the same number. This is fatal
for step 8's order matrix (three random orders, Feature-first), which is nothing but different test
histories.

The fix is entity scoping: an alias is now keyed by (entity, number). The entity comes from
`ride_id` -> `ride`, `rated_user_id` -> `rated_user`, `booking_ids` -> `booking`; from the ENCLOSING
container for a bare `id`, singularised, so `wallet_transactions[].id` and
`wallet_transaction_id` agree; and from the URL segment for an id inside a path, so
`/api/admin/wallet/45/transactions` and `wallet.id` still agree. E-mails keep one global namespace,
because an address identifies one account everywhere. The trade-off is stated in the class docblock
and is real: a relation recorded under a DIFFERENT name than its owner (`data[].id` for a ride,
`ride_id` on its bookings) is now pinned separately, so the corpus claims "same ride" only when both
sides use the same entity name. `tests/Unit/Support/SnapshotNormaliserTest.php` grew to 10 tests /
41 assertions, including one that reproduces the exact collision above.

**DEFECT 2: the fixture's filenames carried the raw row id.** `seedDocumentsFor()` and
`seedProfileFor()` named stored files `documents/snapshot-license-{$user->id}.jpg`, and the committed
corpus had already leaked three different counters into three files - `snapshot-license-733.jpg`,
`snapshot-license-206.jpg` and `snapshot-license-78.jpg` for the same account. The files are now named
after the fixture account's e-mail local part (`snapshot-license-driver.jpg`), which is a fixture
constant.

**DEFECT 3: the ledger leg could not be tied to its transaction.** `ledger_entries.wallet_transaction_id`
was resolved under the entity `wallet_transaction` while the transaction's own `id` resolved under
`wallet_transactions`, so the two never shared a token and the state file's most valuable relation was
invisible. The singularisation rule above fixes it: `wallets[].id` shares a namespace with every
`wallet_id`, and a transaction's `id` with every `wallet_transaction_id`.

**The category report** (`C:\temp\snapshot-diff.php` against a byte copy of the corpus committed in
`cb7e8d7`; 153 cases compared, 124 byte-identical):

| Category | Count | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| STATUS | 0 | no case changed its HTTP status |
| NEW-ITEMS | 0 | no list gained a row; the fixtures are untouched by this step |
| ALIAS | 131 | ids renumbered by the entity-scoping rule (`<id:4>` -> `<id:2>` and back) |
| NULL | 0 | no field changed to or from null |
| NUMBER | 0 | no count, seat or amount changed |
| ANYTHING ELSE | 22 | 14 document/profile filenames de-id-ed (defect 2) + 8 complaint-attachment URLs whose embedded `<id:N>` renumbered (defect 1, inside a URL string) |

No unexplained row: every one of the 22 is the mechanical consequence of a defect fix listed above.

**Verification.** One `SNAPSHOT_UPDATE=1` full regeneration of the snapshot directory:
`OK (163 tests, 864 assertions)`. Then read-only: the whole directory `OK (163 tests, 1500
assertions)`, and - the proof that defect 1 is really fixed - a PARTIAL run of two modules plus the
coverage and emptiness gates `OK (26 tests, 183 assertions)`, which is exactly the composition that
used to rewrite thirteen snapshots. After Pint: a scoped re-run `OK (28 tests, 172 assertions)`.
`pint --test` clean on all six changed/added files, `php -l` clean. No `app/` file was touched.

**Parked for the owner (no app change in this step).** `ledger_entries.wallet_transaction_id` is
never written by any money service: the string appears twice in `app/`, both inside `LedgerEntry`
(the `$fillable` entry and a `belongsTo` that nothing populates), so a ledger leg cannot be traced to
the transaction that produced it. The state snapshots pin it as `null` for every leg and will flag the
day it is populated. Step 4 adds no N+1 of its own; the nine parked from step 3 are untouched.

#### 239.5 Step 5 - the leak guard now watches every base table, not the seven RV45 happened to touch

**What the guard is.** `RefreshDatabase` rolls every test back; one DDL statement (MySQL commits
implicitly) breaks that, and everything the class had inserted becomes permanent. The guard runs
AFTER the rollback, on a fresh connection, and fails the class that leaked. That is how the RV45
pollution turned a fixture in one file into 24 red `CashRideFeeService` tests somewhere else.

**What changed.** `CommittedRowLeakDetector::TABLES` was a hand-written list of the seven tables that
pollution damaged (`wallets`, `users`, `rides`, `bookings`, `user_ratings`, `profile_comments`,
`refresh_tokens`). A leak into any other table was invisible, and "these are the tables that matter"
goes stale the moment a migration adds one. The list is now DERIVED at run time from
`Schema::getTableListing()`, minus one named exclusion:

| Excluded | Reason |
|---|---|
| `migrations` | written by the migration runner OUTSIDE every test transaction, on purpose |

That is the whole exclusion list. Derived on the scratch schema: **30 guarded tables**. The detector
still asks one question in one round trip (a single `SELECT` with one scalar subquery per table),
falls back to per-table counts if a cached table no longer exists - re-deriving the list once first -
and never turns a dead connection into an accusation.

**Cost, measured rather than assumed.** `C:\temp\s05\guard-cost.php` (outside the repo) boots the app
and calls `detect()` 200 times: **1.15 ms per call** over 30 tables, so the whole suite pays roughly
3 seconds for the widened scope.

**The ratchet caught what the widening could not.** `TestDeterminismRatchetTest::no_test_writes_a_tracked_file`
failed on `tests/Support/Snapshots/StateSnapshotRepository.php` (step 4's new writer) because it calls
`file_put_contents()`. The class is legitimate for exactly the reason the response-snapshot repository
is: it writes under `tests/Snapshots`, which IS tracked, and only when `SNAPSHOT_UPDATE=1`. It is now
in `FS_WRITE_ALLOWLIST` with that reason. Worth noting: step 4 never ran the `Review` directory, so
this is the ratchet doing its job on the next pass rather than a defect in the writer.

**Verification - every directory of the suite, because this change is a global invariant.** The guard
runs after EVERY test, so a partial run would prove nothing about the classes it did not run. The
first attempt was a single full-suite job; it died at 32% when the harness restarted and took the
scratch MySQL down with it (the run after the restart was entirely `E` from connection failures - the
detector was never involved). MySQL was restarted once from the documented command, and the suite was
then run in five directory slices that together cover all 25 Feature directories plus Unit:

| Slice | Result |
|---|---|
| Admin, AppFuture, Auth, Bookings, Broadcast, Chat, Complaints, Config, Console, Documents, Notifications, Otp | `OK (416 tests, 1133 assertions)` |
| Payment, Profile, RateLimiting, Repositories, Rides, Security, Staff, T3Batch, T4Batch, Verification, Wallet | `OK (565 tests, 2103 assertions)` |
| Review (118 classes) | `Tests: 654, Assertions: 2253, Skipped: 2` (green; the 2 pre-existing skips) |
| Unit | `OK (987 tests, 1569 assertions)` |
| Snapshots (the whole API corpus) | `OK (163 tests, 1500 assertions)` |

2,785 tests, 2 skipped, zero failures, and **not one committed-row leak reported anywhere** - the
seven tables the old guard watched were already clean, and the other twenty-three are clean too. The
guard component test grew a case that leaks into `notifications` (a table the old seven never
watched) and asserts the derived list equals the schema minus the exclusion, so a future migration
cannot quietly fall outside the guard.

#### 239.6 Step 6 - the ledger properties are randomized: 220 seeded cases, and the seed is printed on every run

**What was there.** `LedgerInvariantsPropertyTest` asserted the four properties (signed legs sum to
zero, money is conserved, escrow is never negative, a replayed movement moves nothing) over FOUR
movements at THREE hand-picked amounts - 50,000, 1,000.50 and 33.33. Twelve cases, chosen by the
person who wrote the fix, which is exactly how a property test stops being a search.

**What was added.** `tests/Support/LedgerPropertySeed.php` generates the scenario set from ONE
integer seed for the whole run: four movements x 55 cases = **220 cases**. Each case draws its own
price in MINOR UNITS (so every amount has exactly two decimals) from five bands that deliberately
include the one-fils boundaries (`0.01`, `1.01`), the single-digit and hundred ranges, and the tens
of thousands; its own seat count (1-3); and, for payout and refund, sometimes a SECOND booking on the
ride, because a collection of one booking cannot catch a bug that only appears when the settlement
loop runs twice.

**Reproducibility is the feature, not a nicety.** `LEDGER_SEED` is honoured if set; otherwise the
seed is drawn once per run and printed to STDERR before the first case:

```
[ledger-seed] seed=619114569 cases=220 - re-run a failure with LEDGER_SEED=619114569
```

Every assertion message carries `seed=<n> case=<index> <movement> price=<p> seats=<n>`, so a red line
is reproducible without re-reading the failure. The four invariants themselves moved into
`tests/Support/Concerns/AssertsLedgerInvariants.php`, used by BOTH property files, so the fixed
anchors and the randomized search cannot drift apart on what "the invariants" are. The random
generator is pure (no database), which is why `tests/Unit/Support/LedgerPropertySeedTest.php` can pin
its contract without a connection: at least 200 cases, four equal movement buckets, the same seed
reproduces the same set, a different seed does not, case names are unique and carry their amount.

**What the randomized layer found on its FIRST run - and it was an assertion, not the app.** Seed
`619114569` produced 22 failures, all of them `payout` cases with a second booking, all with the same
message: `the movement must empty the escrow snapshot, it holds 302770.08`. The test assumed a payout
empties the RIDE; `RidePayout::releaseEscrowToDriver()` settles ONE booking, and the second
passenger's escrow surviving is the correct behaviour. The assertion was corrected, and the case is
now pinned properly: after a per-booking movement the target booking's escrow is empty AND **the
other booking's escrow must still be positive** - a property the fixed-amount test never stated. This
is precisely the failure mode the layer exists for: three fixture amounts had made an over-broad
claim look like a passing test.

**Non-vacuity is explicit.** Four tests break each invariant on purpose (delete a ledger leg; move a
wallet balance alone; set `escrow_held` to -1; replay with a different posting key) and assert that
the property notices. A property layer that cannot fail is a green suite that checks nothing.

**Verification.**

| Run | Seed | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the seed that found the 22 over-broad assertions, after the fix | `619114569` | `OK (220 tests, 2526 assertions)` |
| a fresh random seed | `583514455` | `OK (220 tests, 2534 assertions)` |
| the whole Payment directory | `1` | `OK (271 tests, 2696 assertions)` |
| the guard tests plus the generator unit test | `20261101` | `OK (224 tests, 2548 assertions)` |
| Payment + Review + Unit\Support | `20261101` | `Tests: 943, Assertions: 6342, Skipped: 2` - green after one allowlist entry |
| Review + Unit\Support after the allowlist | `20261101` | `Tests: 668, Assertions: 3621, Skipped: 2` |
| final scoped re-run (both property files + generator tests) | `20261101` | `OK (240 tests, 3986 assertions)` |

`TestDeterminismRatchetTest` flagged `LedgerPropertySeed.php` for `fwrite()` - the same STDERR-only
pattern as `AssertsApiSnapshot`, and it is now in `FS_WRITE_ALLOWLIST` with that reason. No `app/`
file was touched in this step.

#### 239.7 Step 7 - the refusal doors of the money and ride surface are pinned, and they were completely unpinned before

**The gap, measured first.** Before this step the corpus held 153 responses: 123 x 200, 17 x 201, 7 x
400 and 6 x 401. Not one 403, 404, 409 or 422 on any money or ride route - the only error statuses
anywhere came from auth and OTP. A corpus like that documents what success looks like and leaves the
boundary, which is precisely where a client needs to know the code, the message key and the shape of
`errors`.

**16 error-path cases, one new module** (`tests/Feature/Snapshots/ErrorPathSnapshotTest.php`), each a
POST/PATCH/DELETE on a wallet, booking or ride route: 5 wallet, 5 ride, 3 booking, 2 admin, 1 staff.

| Case | Status | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `wallet/request-withdraw-more-than-balance` | 422 | `Insufficient balance. Your current balance is...` |
| `wallet/request-charge-zero-amount` | 422 | `The amount field must be at least 1.` (`errors`) |
| `wallet/requests-store-unknown-type` | 422 | `The selected type is invalid.` (`errors`) |
| `wallet/create-direct-already-has-a-wallet` | **409** | `You already have a wallet.` |
| `wallet/requests-destroy-not-the-owner` | **404** | `Request not found.` |
| `rides/book-without-the-balance` | 422 | the generic masked message (see below) |
| `rides/book-more-seats-than-the-ride-has` | 422 | `Not enough seats available. Requested: 5, Av...` |
| `rides/book-the-drivers-own-ride` | 422 | `Drivers cannot book their own rides` |
| `rides/cancel-someone-elses-trip` | **422** | `Only the ride creator can cancel it` |
| `rides/create-departure-in-the-past` | 422 | `Departure time must be at least 5 minutes in...` |
| `bookings/accept-someone-elses-request` | **422** | the generic masked message |
| `bookings/cancel-someone-elses-booking` | **422** | the generic masked message |
| `bookings/cancel-more-seats-than-booked` | 422 | `Cannot cancel 5 seat(s). You have 2 seat(s)...` |
| `admin/wallet-charge-a-negative-amount` | 422 | `errors` + `code` + `status` |
| `admin/passenger-charge-a-negative-amount` | 422 | `errors` + `status` |
| `staff/bookings-cancel-a-booking-that-does-not-exist` | 404 | `Booking not found.` |

The five bold statuses are where the case-writing guess was wrong and the APP was right: the first
generation run refused to write those files and named the real status in its message, so the corpus
records behaviour rather than preference. All 16 are POST/PATCH/DELETE, so all 16 are also in
`MONEY_AND_RIDE_MUTATION_CASES` and pin their ROWS: the state twins prove a refusal did not write the
booking it refused, move a balance or touch escrow.

**The refusals are cheap, and that is now pinned.** The 16 new query budgets are 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2,
4, 4, 4, 5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 10 queries - a validation refusal refuses before doing work. The budget diff
is 16 added lines and ZERO changed lines, so no existing case's budget moved.

**Parked findings from this batch (no app change).**

1. `POST /api/rides/{ride}/book` answers an INSUFFICIENT BALANCE with the same generic 422
   `The request could not be completed. Please try again.` that an authorization refusal uses. A
   passenger whose wallet is short cannot tell that from "you may not do this at all", and neither can
   a client deciding whether to offer a top-up.
2. `POST /api/bookings/{id}/accept` and `/cancel` answer a foreign actor's attempt with the same
   generic 422 instead of 403/404, so an authorization failure is reported as a validation failure.
   Leaking less about another user's booking is defensible; reporting it as "try again" is not,
   because retrying cannot succeed.
3. The error `errors` envelope is not uniform: admin routes answer `{code, errors, status}`, wallet
   validation answers `{errors, message}`, wallet business refusals answer
   `{message, status, success}`, and booking/ride refusals answer `{message, success}`. Documented by
   the snapshots rather than changed.

#### 239.8 Step 8 (final) - the order matrix found a real order dependence, and the corpus is now frozen by a manifest

**Part 1: the order matrix.** The same selection - the whole 179-case corpus, the money suite and the
snapshot support unit tests, 474 tests - was run five times in five execution orders, with a
leftover-row probe against all 30 guarded tables after each run:

| Run | Order | Result | Leftover rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `--order-by=default` (Payment, then the corpus, then Unit) | `OK (474 tests, 6143 assertions)` | clean |
| 2 | `--order-by=reverse` (corpus FIRST, then Payment, then Unit) | **FAILED** - `admin/routes-popular` (see below) | clean |
| 3 | `--order-by=random --random-order-seed=1` | `OK (474 tests, 6142 assertions)` | clean |
| 4 | `--order-by=random --random-order-seed=20261101` | `OK (474 tests, 6148 assertions)` | clean |
| 5 | `--order-by=random --random-order-seed=999983` | `OK (474 tests, 6137 assertions)` | clean |

**The reverse order was red, and that is the value of the matrix.** `admin/routes-popular` answered
Hama/Latakia/Homs in four orders and Homs-first in the fifth: `AdminTripService::getPopularRoutes()`
groups by (pickup_address, destination_address) and sorts by EXACTLY ONE key, `trip_count`, with no
tiebreaker - and the fixture put Homs, Latakia and Hama at one trip each, so all three rows tied on
the only sort key and MySQL was free to return them in any order. Step 3 had already met this flake
and thought it had fixed it with a second passenger on Homs; `total_passengers` is displayed but
never sorted on, so the tie never went away. An intermittent red that four runs out of five cannot
reproduce is exactly what makes a corpus untrustworthy, and nothing short of a different execution
order would have found it.

**The fix, and its limits.** `tests/` only, so the fixture now gives the three live trips distinct
trip counts - Latakia twice, Homs once, plus the four Damascus -> Aleppo rides (4 / 2 / 1). The
endpoint's one sort key is then unique per row and the ranking is deterministic and worth pinning.
The diff is confined to the destination string and its consequences: 10 response files, one line
each except `routes-popular` (Hama disappears, Latakia becomes trip_count 2 / 50% / "High"). No
state snapshot changed - `captureMoneyAndRideState()` does not pin destinations. The corpus was
regenerated ONCE, deliberately, and the manifest refreshed in the same commit.

The fixture invariant is now guarded rather than remembered:
`SnapshotEmptinessTest::the_popular_routes_snapshot_can_actually_pin_its_ordering` fails if the
committed list ever contains two equal `trip_count` values (or is not ordered by it descending), so a
future fixture edit that reintroduces the tie turns into a deterministic red at regeneration time
instead of somebody else's intermittent failure. **The real fix is a tiebreaker in
`AdminTripService::getPopularRoutes()`; it is PARKED because `app/` is frozen in this batch.**

Bonus coverage from the five orders: `LedgerPropertySeed` drew a different random seed in each run
(634087025, 140910540, 98509883, 655798503, 403097770), so the matrix also executed **1,100 fresh
randomized ledger cases**, all green. That is why the assertion counts differ slightly between rows of
the table: some randomized cases carry a second booking and assert more. Test COUNT is identical
(474) - which is the number that matters.

**Part 2: the freeze.** `tests/Snapshots/MANIFEST.json` records every committed corpus file and its
sha256: **211 files** (169 response snapshots, 40 state snapshots, `query-budgets.json`,
`route-inventory.json`). `SnapshotFreezeTest` (5 tests) compares it in BOTH directions - changed hash,
missing file, extra file - and names the files. The per-case comparisons only cover the cases a run
actually executes; the manifest catches a snapshot deleted or renamed in a module the run never
touched, which is the "structural commit quietly shrinks the corpus" failure this freeze exists for.

The freeze never repairs itself: `SnapshotManifest` writes only through
`scripts/refresh-snapshot-manifest.php` (a new, documented script outside `tests/`) and the test that
reads it is read-only, because a freeze that regenerates itself is not a freeze. Both commands are
printed inside every failure message:

```
SNAPSHOT_UPDATE=1 php vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Feature/Snapshots   # rewrite the corpus
php scripts/refresh-snapshot-manifest.php                          # rewrite the manifest
```

`TestDeterminismRatchetTest` flagged the new writer for `file_put_contents()`, as it should; it is in
`FS_WRITE_ALLOWLIST` with the reason that it writes the tracked manifest and only from that script.

**Verification.**

|---|---|
| gate run 1 (before the fix): five orders | reverse FAILED on `admin/routes-popular`, other four green, leftover rows clean |
| gate run 2 (after the fix and the manifest refresh): five orders | **`OK` in all five** (474 tests each), leftover rows clean after every run |
| `tests/Feature/Review` (118 classes) after every step-8 file change | green - see the step's commit note |
| freeze non-vacuity: hash-tampered `api/rides/book-without-the-balance.json` | named, with the refresh command |
| freeze non-vacuity: deleted `state/rides/book.json` | `The manifest freezes state/rides/book.json, which does not exist.` |
| freeze non-vacuity: added `api/wallet/__freeze_probe.json` | `on disk but not frozen by the manifest: api/wallet/__freeze_probe.json` |
| `pint --test` on the changed files | PASS |

### 240. Stage 0.6 - the performance batch (owner's five items)

#### 240.1 Item 1 - the nine "N+1 routes": three were real, two were already batched, four are a fixture artefact that the freeze forbids fixing

Item 1 of the owner's stage 0.6 list asked for the nine N+1 signatures parked in 239.3 to be eager
loaded, each budget re-recorded DOWN, with **no response change**. The first thing this item did was
measure instead of assume: a temporary probe (`tests/Feature/Snapshots/NPlusOneProbeTest.php`, deleted
before the commit - see the proof at the end of this section) re-ran the nine cases through the real
harness and printed every query each one issued. That turned the nine into three groups, and the
split is the finding: **the step-3 "N+1 signature" was inferred from budget deltas, and four of the
nine were never the app's queries at all.**

**Group 1 - fixed (3 cases). All responses byte-identical.**

| Case | Was | Now | What was per-row |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chat/messages-index` | 10 | **8** | `ChatMessageHandler::formatMessage()` reads `$message->sender` and its **profile photo** for every row; `ChatRepository::getMessages()` eager-loaded `sender` but not `sender.profile`, so `getUserProfilePhoto()` took its documented fallback `Profile::where('user_id', ...)` once per message. Now `->with('sender.profile')` - one batched profile query. |
| `admin/drivers` | 15 | **9** | Two lookups ran once PER DRIVER: `UserRating::where('rated_user_id', ...)->avg('rating')` in a `transform()`, and `AdminDriverPresenter::resolveDriverPhone()` (`Ride::where('driver_id', ...)->whereNotNull(...)->orderByDesc('created_at')->value(...)`). Now `withAvg('receivedRatings as avg_rating', 'rating')` plus a correlated `latest_communication_number` subquery on the list query; the presenter prefers that attribute when the caller materialised it (`array_key_exists`, so a NULL number does not trigger a redundant query) and keeps its own query on every other path. |
| `admin/passenger-full-profile` | 22 | **20** | `buildWalletCharges($userId)` re-read the user AND its wallet (`User::with('wallet')->find()`) even though `fullProfile()` had just loaded both via `profileBundle()`. The builder now takes an optional already-loaded user; the standalone `/wallet-charges` endpoint passes nothing and is unchanged (still 11). |

A fourth case improved for free: `staff/chat-messages` 14 -> **13** (same message formatter, same
missing profile eager load).

**Group 2 - no N+1 left to fix (2 cases).** `admin/dashboard-recent` (9) and
`admin/passenger-wallet-charges` (11) measure exactly their budget, and the probe shows every related
read already batched (`... where id in (50, 54)`, `... where user_id in (63)`): there is no per-row
query in either. The "+1 each" in 239.3 was the enriched fixture, not an N+1. Nothing to re-record.

**Group 3 - PARKED, four cases: the queries are the fixture's, and removing them changes the
response.** `rides/index` (15), `rides/search-get` (10), `rides/search-post` (10) and
`admin/trips-live` (16) spend 10 / 6 / 6 / 6 queries on
`SELECT ST_AsText(pickup_location|destination_location) AS wkt FROM rides WHERE id = ?` - two per
ride. That is `Ride::getPickupLocationAttribute()`'s documented **fallback** path (RV-24): the
accessor reads the scalar `pickup_lat/pickup_lng/destination_lat/destination_lng` columns and only
queries the geometry when they are NULL. They are NULL because `RideBuilder` inserts rides with a raw
`DB::raw` geometry expression and deliberately bypasses the model mutators - `RV24RideCoordinateReadTest`
PINS that ("precondition: a raw RideBuilder insert has no scalar lat (it is the fallback case)").
Production rows are never in that state: the mutator writes the scalars on create and the backfill
migration (`2026_10_05_000001_backfill_ride_lat_lng_from_geometry`) covers legacy rows.

So the fix is a fixture change, and it was implemented and measured: a `withScalarCoordinates()`
opt-in on `RideBuilder` (writing the four scalar columns from the accessor's OWN lat-first parse of
the same WKT, so fast path and fallback are equal by construction) applied at the harness's four ride
creation sites. **Measured result: 15 -> 5, 10 -> 4, 10 -> 4, 16 -> 10 - and four response snapshots
changed**, because those endpoints serialize the raw model (`select *` plus `toArray()`), so the
scalar columns ARE part of the JSON:

```
api/rides/index.json        "destination_lat": null -> "36.20210000"
                            "pickup_lat": null      -> "33.51380000"     (the same four fields in
api/rides/search-get.json   ...                                        rides/cancel.json and
api/rides/search-post.json  ...                                        rides/search-post.json)
api/rides/cancel.json       ...
```

The `pickup_location`/`destination_location` OBJECTS were byte-identical, which independently
confirms the two paths agree. But item 1 says "no response change" and the stage-0.5 freeze says
response snapshots must stay byte-identical, so **the fixture change was reverted in full** (builder
opt-in, the four call sites, and the four regenerated snapshots) and the four budgets were left at
their measured truth. The owner's question is in 240.4.

Verification of item 1: the probe output is in the run log; the corpus was regenerated ONCE
(`SNAPSHOT_UPDATE=1`), and `git status` on `tests/Snapshots` shows **only `query-budgets.json`**, so
all 169 response snapshots and all 40 state snapshots are byte-identical. The manifest was refreshed
in the same commit (`changed 1`). `git status` also proves the probe is gone:
`tests/Feature/Snapshots/NPlusOneProbeTest.php` does not exist and is not in any commit.
`pint --test` PASS, `php -l` clean, and the battery below is green.

#### 240.2 Item 2 - `GET /api/score/transactions` no longer 500s on a row that references a Ride or a Booking, and the reference VALUES are pinned

**The defect, reproduced before touching anything.** `ScoreTransactionResource::formatRide()` read
`$ride->origin` and `$ride->destination`, and `formatBooking()` read the same two names on the nested
ride. The Ride model has no such attributes (it stores `pickup_address` / `destination_address`), and
the app arms `preventAccessingMissingAttributes` outside production, so the read THREW and the whole
endpoint answered 500. It stayed invisible because none of the world's score rows carried a
reference: `hydrateReferences()` never attached a `referenceModel`, `buildReference()` returned
`id + type` only, and both formatters were unreachable. A new case that seeds the two reference
shapes proved it on the first run - the harness refused to write a snapshot and reported the app's
real answer:

```
Refusing to snapshot 'score/transactions-with-ride-and-booking-references':
  the case documents status 200 but the call returned 500.
  Body starts: {"status":"error","message":"An unexpected error occurred.","code":500}
```

**The fix is two attribute names, and the JSON keys do not move** - the response keeps `origin` /
`destination`, which is the shape the resource's own docblock documents; only the attribute they are
read FROM changes. `formatRide()` now reads `pickup_address` / `destination_address`, and
`formatBooking()`'s nested `ride` block does the same.

**What the new case pins, and what it cannot.** `score/transactions-with-ride-and-booking-references`
seeds the two shapes through the REAL score service, with the app's own reference-bearing calls:

- `ScoreService::recordRideCompleted($ride)` awards `RIDE_COMPLETED` with `reference: $ride` to the
  driver AND to every passenger holding a COMPLETED booking on the ride - so the standard booking is
  completed first, exactly as the endpoint is read in production.
- `ScoreService::recordPassengerNoShow($passenger, $booking, 'cash')` awards `PASSENGER_NO_SHOW` with
  `reference: $booking` (cash, so the -15 really applies; e-pay overrides the points to 0).

Verified log evidence: `{"passenger_no_show", -15, reference Booking}` and `{"ride_completed", +10,
reference Ride}` in the same page, the first with a nested `ride` block (the booking-reference shape)
and the second without it (the ride-reference shape) - both branches of `buildReference()`.

**The snapshot pins the SHAPE, not the VALUES, and that gap is closed by a second test.**
`reference` is one of the normaliser's `ID_KEYS`, and the normaliser forces the id family onto every
scalar inside it, so `reference.origin` and `reference.destination` are aliased to `<id:N>` (the same
is true of the existing corpus - it is pre-existing behaviour, deliberately untouched because
changing it would rewrite snapshots the freeze protects). A mapping that swapped origin for
destination would therefore still produce a byte-identical snapshot. So
`tests/Feature/Review/ScoreTransactionReferenceValuesTest.php` (2 tests, 17 assertions) hits the same
endpoint and asserts the real text against the rows it came from: the ride reference's
`origin`/`destination` are the ride's `pickup_address`/`destination_address` and are NOT equal to each
other, and the booking reference carries its own id, its status, and a nested ride block with the
same two addresses.

**State coverage.** The case declares `'state' => 'score'` (a new value for the harness's existing
per-case `state` knob), which captures the rows behind a score response: `score_transactions`
(action, points, previous/new score, `reference_type`, `reference_id`, reason) and `user_scores`
(score, total_rides, total_cancellations). The committed state file proves the fixture is real - one
row with `reference_type = App\Models\Ride` shared by the driver's and the passenger's award (SAME
`<id:7>` alias, so the snapshot pins "one ride, two awards"), and one with `reference_type =
App\Models\Booking` pointing at the booking. `captureMoneyAndRideState()` is untouched, so no existing
state file moved.

**Freeze compliance, measured.** The regeneration wrote exactly two new files and one changed file:

```
?? tests/Snapshots/api/score/transactions-with-ride-and-booking-references.json     (new case)
?? tests/Snapshots/state/score/transactions-with-ride-and-booking-references.json   (new state twin)
 M tests/Snapshots/query-budgets.json                                              (+ "score/transactions-...": 5)
```

`git status` on `tests/Snapshots` shows no other file, so all 169 existing response snapshots and all
40 existing state snapshots are byte-identical. The manifest refresh reports
`Frozen files: 213 (added 2, removed 0, changed 1)`.

Verification: `tests/Feature/Snapshots` + the new value test -> `OK (188 tests, 2080 assertions)`; the
item-2 area floor (`tests/Feature/Review`, `tests/Feature/Rides`, `tests/Unit/Models`) ->
`Tests: 912, Assertions: 2712, Skipped: 2`, exit 0, no failures.
#### 240.3 Item 3 - `AdminTripService::getPopularRoutes()` gets a deterministic tiebreaker, and the tie path gets a test the frozen snapshot cannot provide

**The finding (carried from stage 0.5 step 8).** `GET /api/admin/routes/popular` grouped by
`(pickup_address, destination_address)` and sorted by exactly one key, `trip_count`. Two destinations
with the same count were therefore returned in whatever order MySQL's grouping happened to produce:
the step-8 order matrix answered `Hama/Latakia/Homs` in four execution orders and `Homs`-first in the
fifth. The committed snapshot only stopped flapping because the fixture was changed to give the three
live trips DISTINCT counts (Aleppo 4, Latakia 2, Homs 1), with a DB-free guard
(`SnapshotEmptinessTest::the_popular_routes_snapshot_can_actually_pin_its_ordering`) that fails at
regeneration time if a tie ever comes back.

**The fix** is one line: `->orderBy('rides.destination_address')` after `->orderByDesc('trip_count')`.
`destination_address` is a grouping column, so ordering by it is stable, and it only ever decides
ties - the primary ranking is untouched.

**The frozen snapshot did not move.** Ordering by a second key cannot reorder rows that differ on the
first key, and the fixture has no ties, so `admin/routes-popular.json` is byte-identical;
`git status --short tests/Snapshots` is empty after the change. Re-verified before the commit.

**Why the corpus cannot protect this, and what does.** The fixture guard exists precisely to make the
corpus tie-free, so no committed snapshot can ever exercise the tie path - that is what a
characterization test is for. `tests/Feature/Review/AdminPopularRoutesTieBreakTest.php` builds one
clear leader (Aleppo, twice) and a THREE-way tie at one trip each (Hama, Homs, Latakia), then asserts
the response order is `Aleppo, Hama, Homs, Latakia` with counts `2, 1, 1, 1`, and that two identical
requests answer identical documents.

**Non-vacuity, proven by a wrong fix.** A tiebreaker test can look green by luck (that was the whole
bug), so the test was checked against a deliberately WRONG tiebreaker: flipping it to
`orderByDesc('rides.destination_address')` turned it red (`Failed asserting that two arrays are
identical`, `Tests: 1, Failures: 1`), and restoring the ascending order turned it green again
(`OK (1 test, 5 assertions)`). The test therefore constrains the tiebreaker's direction, not MySQL's
mood.

**Stale comments corrected (documentation only, no assertion touched).** Two fixtures still claimed
this work was "parked because app/ is frozen": the `$liveTrips` comment in
`tests/Feature/Snapshots/ApiSnapshotTestCase.php` and the guard's docblock in
`SnapshotEmptinessTest.php`. Both now state that the app-side tiebreaker landed and that the tie path
is pinned by the Review test; the same file's comment about the score reference defect (item 2) was
corrected at the same time, since it also described a parked defect that is now fixed.

Verification: `tests/Feature/Review/AdminPopularRoutesTieBreakTest.php` + `tests/Feature/Admin` ->
`OK (123 tests, 270 assertions)`, and `tests/Feature/Snapshots` -> `OK (188 tests, 2080 assertions)`
after the comment edits.

#### 240.4 Item 4 - the five parked findings, each with the evidence as it stands TODAY and the question for the owner

No app code, no snapshot, no test changed in this item: each of these needs a decision, and three of
them would change a frozen response or a frozen state file. The evidence below was re-measured against
the working tree at this commit, not quoted from an earlier record - and one of the five came back
DIFFERENT from what the earlier record said, which is recorded as such.

**Parked 1 - a refusal is reported as a validation failure (422 instead of 403/404).**
Measured straight off the frozen corpus (11 of the 28 error responses are 4xx refusals):

| Case | Answers | Should read as |
|---|---|---|
| `bookings/accept-someone-elses-request` | 422 `{message, success}` | 403/404 - the caller is not the booking's owner |
| `bookings/cancel-someone-elses-booking` | 422 `{message, success}` | 403/404 |
| `rides/cancel-someone-elses-trip` | 422 `{message, status}` | 403/404 |
| `rides/book-the-drivers-own-ride` | 422 `{message, success}` | 403/404 (a driver booking their own ride) |
| `rides/book-without-the-balance` | 422 `{message, success}` | 422 is defensible, but the MESSAGE is the generic "The request could not be completed. Please try again." - the same text an authorization refusal uses, so a client cannot tell "top up your wallet" from "you may never do this" |
| `bookings/cancel-more-seats-than-booked` | 422 `{message, status}` | correct as-is (genuine validation) |
| `staff/bookings-cancel-a-booking-that-does-not-exist` | 404 `{message, status}` | correct as-is - so 404 IS already used elsewhere |

*Why it is parked:* every one of those bodies is a frozen response snapshot; changing a status or a
message rewrites five committed files, which this batch's freeze forbids. It is also a decision, not a
fix: 404-for-a-foreign-row hides the row's existence, 403 admits it exists.
*Question for the owner:* for a foreign booking/ride, should the API answer 403 (the row exists, you
may not touch it) or 404 (pretend it does not exist)? And on the insufficient-balance path, may I
replace the generic "try again" message with a balance-specific one (422 kept), given that the message
text is itself pinned by a snapshot?

**Parked 2 - the error envelope has eleven different shapes.**
Measured by grouping every one of the 28 committed 4xx/5xx corpus responses by its top-level keys:

| Status | Responses | Top-level keys |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | 7 | `message + success` |
| 401 | 6 | `code + message + status` |
| 404 | 1 | `message + status` |
| 404 | 1 | `message + status + success` |
| 409 | 1 | `message + success` |
| 422 | 5 | `message + success` |
| 422 | 3 | `errors + message` |
| 422 | 2 | `message + status` |
| 422 | 1 | `errors + status` |
| 422 | 1 | `message + status + success` |
| 422 | 1 | `code + errors + status` |

`success` appears on some refusals and not others, `code` on the 401s and one 422 only, `errors` on four
shapes only, and `status` is sometimes the HTTP code and sometimes absent. A client cannot write one
error handler against this.
*Why it is parked:* unifying it rewrites essentially every error snapshot in the corpus (28+ files) -
the largest possible violation of the freeze - and it is a public response-shape change, which the
standing rules forbid without an explicit decision.
*Question for the owner:* do you want ONE envelope for every non-2xx (if so, which: `{status, message,
code?, errors?}`?), or is the current per-surface shape deliberate? If you want it unified, it must be a
separate batch with an explicit freeze exemption for the error snapshots.

**Parked 3 - `POST /api/profile` hides the caller's OWN documents.**
`ProfileController::profileUpdateResponse()` (line 348) calls
`formatProfileData($result['profile'], $result['user'])` without the third argument, which defaults to
`false`, and `ownerDocuments($user, false)` returns `[]`. The caller of `POST /api/profile` is always
the owner of the profile being updated, so the response should carry the documents the owner is allowed
to see - `GET /api/profile/{ownId}` passes `true` explicitly (line 82) and would show them.
Evidence: the world gives the standard passenger four documents (`face_id`, `back_id`, `license`,
`mechanic_card`), and `profile/update.json` answers `"documents": []` for that passenger, while
`admin/driver-profile.json` shows a populated `documents` block for the driver. The same user, in the
same session, sees their documents on one route and not on the other.
*Why it is parked:* `profile/update` is a frozen response snapshot, and the fix ADDS data to a response
body (`documents` `[]` -> four entries). It is the one-line `true` argument; it is not the ambiguity
that stops me, the freeze is.
*Question for the owner:* confirm the intent - should the profile-update response carry the owner's

|---|---|

| Committed ledger legs in the state corpus | 603 |
| Legs whose `wallet_transaction_id` is non-null | 2 (both in `state/admin/wallet-charge.json`) |

So the column is real and load-bearing on one path and empty on 601 of 603 legs: on every escrow hold,

an in-progress migration rather than an oversight.

the batch rules forbid.
*Question for the owner:* is the intent that every converted money path keeps passing its

**Parked 5 - the four ride-list "N+1 signatures" are a fixture artefact, and the fix changes four frozen responses (new in this batch).**

path (a legacy row without scalars must still resolve), so the queries are not dead code - they are

*Why it is parked:* the measured fix was to write scalar coordinates in `RideBuilder`

*Question for the owner:* the fixture can be made to match production (the model mutator writes those

freeze exemption for those four files, (b) the scalar coordinate columns hidden from the API so the
response never carries them (a response-shape change, and the fallback stays), or (c) the four budgets
kept as they are and the finding left as documentation that the fixture is the reason?

### 241. Stage 1, phase 1 - five module providers, the 34 ports move into their modules' Contracts, and a boundary ratchet that cannot pass vacuously

**Owner's goal (new batch, same REFACTORING MODE):** real modules under
`app/Modules/{Communication,Money,Ride,Identity,Console}`, namespace `App\Modules\<Name>\`, layout
`{Http/Controllers,Http/Handlers,Services,Repositories,Domain,Contracts,Providers}`. Phase 1 is the
part that moves NO module code: (a) one `<Name>ServiceProvider` per module taking that module's
bindings out of `Support/ContainerBindings` with identical lifetimes, (b) every port out of
`app/Interfaces` into the Contracts namespace of the module that IMPLEMENTS it, (c) a
`ModuleBoundaryTest`. Phases 2 (one commit per module, in the order Communication, Money, Ride,
Identity, Console) and 3 (five-order matrix + leftover-rows probe over the full suite) follow.

Per-commit hard rules for the whole batch: `tests/Snapshots` byte-identical (no `SNAPSHOT_UPDATE=1`),
`MANIFEST.json` unchanged, query budgets unchanged, the leak guard clean, whole-tree Pint clean, and
the default-order full suite green.

`app/Support/ContainerBindings.php` was the whole container catalogue in one body (386 lines, **75

**Parity is measured, not asserted by hand.** `C:\temp\s05\binding-parity.php` reads the HEAD version
out of `git show` and the union of the five providers plus the remnant, extracts each registration's
`(kind, key, target)` triple (closure targets normalised to a marker), and compares the sorted sets:

```
HEAD registrations: 75
now  registrations: 75
IDENTICAL binding catalogue (kind, key, target)
```

**The old promise changed, deliberately.** The file's docblock used to say binding order was
"byte-for-byte unchanged" - that described batch 227, which moved the body without regrouping it.
Regrouping by module necessarily reorders registrations. It cannot matter here, and the reason is
checkable rather than assumed: in phase 1(b) each port went to the module that IMPLEMENTS it, so every
`bind(Port::class, Impl::class)` now sits in the same provider as the singleton it resolves to, and no
binding can depend on one that another module registers. The docblock, `config/app.php` and both new
comments say this instead of the old claim. `config/app.php` registers the five providers after
`HorizonServiceProvider`, in the modules' own order.

#### 241.3 Phase 1(c) - `tests/Feature/AppFuture/ModuleBoundaryTest.php` (6 tests, baseline 0)

Five rules, each with the number it measured on 2026-11-02:

* A. a MODULE file may name its own module, any module's `Contracts`, and the kernel - never another
  module's implementation. **Measured: 0.**
* B. a KERNEL file may name module `Contracts` (that is what ports are for) - never module
  implementation. **Measured: 0.**
* C. ENTRYPOINTS (artisan commands, `Http/Middleware`, `Providers`, `Support/ContainerBindings`) are
  the wiring layer and are exempt from B, but the exemption is a named, exact list at its measured
  count. **Measured: 1 file** - `Console/Commands/CleanupExpiredOtps.php`, which resolves an Identity
  port. The container catalogue is NOT on the list any more: it registers shared kernel bindings only,
  so phase 1 narrowed the exemption rather than widening it.
* D. the kernel's use of module `Contracts` is a **transitional ceiling**: 87 files today, because the
  ports moved to their modules while their callers (controllers, services, repositories) are still
  kernel files. Phase 2 moves those callers into their modules, where naming another module's Contracts
  is the sanctioned edge, so the number falls toward the handful of kernel files that legitimately
  remain; each phase-2 commit lowers the ceiling to the newly measured number.
* E. anti-vacuity floors, so no move can make the rules pass by scanning nothing: the scan must see at
  least 351 app files (the tree has 351), every module must keep at least its measured file count
  (Communication 5, Money 9, Ride 7, Identity 13, Console 5), and every module must keep its
  `<Name>ServiceProvider`.

**Interpretation decision, for the owner to correct if wrong.** "The kernel may not import a module"
is implemented as: the kernel may not import module IMPLEMENTATION; `<Module>\Contracts` is the
published boundary, and kernel wiring files may use it (rule D bounds how many). The stricter reading
- the kernel may not name a module at all - would make the ports unusable from the kernel and would
fail on 87 files today, most of which phase 2 moves into modules anyway.

`PostingKey` were placed in `Modules/Money/Domain/` on the reasoning that posting-keys are domain
concepts. `BoundaryDependencyTest` immediately failed: `domain_to_models` (baseline 0, never raised)
reported `Modules/Money/Domain/PostingKey.php`, because that file reads `App\Models\WalletTransaction`.
A domain file that touches Eloquent is exactly what that rule forbids, and the rule was right: the pair
belongs with the services, so they moved to `Modules/Money/Services/` and the violation disappeared.
The audit records it because the alternative - quietly relaxing a baseline - is the failure mode the
whole batch exists to prevent.

**Rule B needed no work this time.** No kernel file named a Money implementation after the move (the
batch-233 ports already carried every cross-context money call), so the kernel->Contracts ceiling fell
from 82 files to **71** and the module floor rose from 9 to **35**.

**Path-based tests re-pointed (mechanical only, no assertion touched).**
`MoneyRoundingIsDecidedInOnePlaceTest` pinned seven `app/Services/Payment/*.php` paths; they now name
`app/Modules/Money/Services/*.php` (the test's whole purpose is to prove rounding is decided in one
place, so it has to look at where that place is now). `RV28InfraHardeningTest`'s
"primary-only reads still force the write PDO" list named `app/Http/Controllers/API/WalletController.php`;
it now names the module's controller. `CrossContextBoundaryTest`'s `Support/FeeSplit.php` /
`Support/PostingKey.php` branch became unreachable (the module prefix covers them), so it was removed
and the docblock updated to the new MONEY paths. `BoundaryDependencyTest` and
`CrossContextBoundaryTest` needed no further change: the layer-aware classification and the
`Modules/<Name>/` context mapping added with the Communication commit already see these files, which
is why all nine layer baselines and all 20 ordered pairs are still at their recorded numbers.

**One defect of my own, caught and fixed inside this commit.**
`C:\temp\s05\relocate.php` (the helper that moves a file *within* a module) tested the moved file's
new path against a map keyed by old paths, so it rewrote the FQCN references but not the file's own
`namespace` line. The money-area run failed instantly with
`Cannot declare class App\Modules\Money\Domain\PostingKey ... in .../Services/PostingKey.php`, which is
the good kind of failure: loud, immediate, and impossible to mistake for a pass. Both namespaces were
rewritten from their paths, `composer dump-autoload --no-scripts` re-run, and the same 526-test
selection re-run green.

tests, `tests/Feature/Wallet`, `tests/Feature/Payment`, `tests/Unit/Domain`): 526 tests, 3409
assertions, OK. Whole-tree Pint: 8 fixes, all import order (plus one pre-existing style file that the
move rewrote), then PASS over 778 files. Snapshot corpus untouched; the leak guard is inside the full
run below.

#### 243.a The scanners that would have gone quietly blind (and the inventory that stops it recurring)

The first full-suite run of this commit failed with 3 errors - all of them path-pinning tests that had
been reading files which moved. That is the loud, harmless kind. The dangerous kind is the *ceiling*
tests: they count matches under a directory or a file list and assert `count <= N`, so when the files
move away the count simply falls and the test passes while no longer looking at anything. Two of them
were reading the controller tree and would have lost the module's controllers permanently:

* `RV13ExceptionCodeAsStatusTest::no_controller_uses_an_exception_code_as_an_http_status` swept
  `app_path('Http/Controllers')` only. It now uses a `controllerFiles()` helper that reads that
  directory plus `glob(app_path('Modules/*/Http/Controllers'))`. It is the same file set as before the
  moves.
* `ExceptionMessageLeakRatchetTest` did the same in `leaks()` and in the server-side-logging probe
  (two `RecursiveDirectoryIterator` loops). Both now read `controllerFiles()`; the leak count is a
  `array_sum(array_map('count', ...))`, so the added module controllers cannot change the ordering
  assumptions of any assertion.
* `RV33BoundaryDependencyTest::payment_method_branching_outside_the_domain_only_decreases` exempted
  files under `/Domain/Payment/`. After the move the money domain is `Modules/Money/Domain/`, so the
  exemption silently stopped applying and the ceiling would have been measuring the very layer it
  exists to exempt. It now exempts both spellings.

Re-pointed outright because they name a file that moved (mechanical, no assertion touched):
`MoneyRoundingIsDecidedInOnePlaceTest` (7 `app/Services/Payment/*` paths),
`RV28InfraHardeningTest` (`WalletController`), `RV13ExceptionCodeAsStatusTest` (2 x
`app_path('Services/Wallet/WalletRequestService.php')`), `RV19FeeSplitTest` (5 x
`app_path('Services/Payment/*.php')`), and `CrossContextBoundaryTest` (the now-unreachable
`Support/FeeSplit.php` / `Support/PostingKey.php` branch).

**Inventory for the modules still to move** (found by sweeping `tests/` for path literals and directory
sweeps; each must be re-pointed in the commit that moves its file, never left pointing at a directory
that no longer holds it):

| Test | Path it reads | Moves with |
|---|---|---|
| `RV11ScoreLedgerTest` (3 sites) | `app_path('Services/Score/ScoreLedger.php')`, `.../ScoreService.php` | Ride |
| `RV16EnumerationUniformityTest:204` | `glob(app_path('Http/Controllers/API/*Controller.php'))`, filtered to the four auth controllers | Identity |
| `RV16SignupMailAfterCommitTest` (2 sites) | `app_path('Http/Controllers/API/Support/SignupRegistrationHandler.php')` | Identity |
| `TlsAndOctaneHygieneTest:107` | `app_path('Services/WhatsAppOtpService.php')` | Identity |
| `WaveZeroVerificationTest:268` | `app_path('Repositories/VerificationRepository.php')` | Identity |
| `RV19FeeSplitTest:186` | `app_path('Services/Admin/AdminDriverService.php')` | Console |
| `WaveZeroVerificationTest:248` | `app_path('Services/Admin/AdminReportService.php')` | Console |
| `T48CommentEncodingTest` (9 pinned paths) | the profile/KYC comment-encoding files | Identity |
